# v3.8 — CSS Grid Layout Techniques CSS Grid is the modern way to create complex, responsive layouts. Here are the key techniques used in qbit-notes: ## 1. Auto-fit Responsive Grid ```css .demo-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: var(--grid-size); } → Perfect for card galleries and responsive panels. Explicit Named Grid Areas (Nuke-style Layout) CSS.explicit-grid { display: grid; grid-template-areas: "header header" "sidebar main" "footer footer"; grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr; } → Ideal for complex orchestrator panels with fixed sidebar + flexible main area. Output • Render Queue 3. 20px Grid Snapping (Node Graph Foundation) CSS.node-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 1fr); gap: var(--grid-size); } → Used for precise block placement in the orchestrator canvas. Read Clean Key Merge 4. Combining Grid + Flex The main layout uses display:flex for the overall page while inner sections use Grid for precise control. Pro Tips: Use var(--grid-size) for consistent spacing auto-fit makes layouts responsive Named areas make complex UIs readable and maintainable Grid works perfectly with absolute positioned blocks (our node graph) Copy any example above and paste into the editor to see live updates.
